data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's evidence criterion ('divergence-convergence' in panel notes) fails to distinguish genuine reliability gain from mere compliance. A panel can exhibit surface divergence (disagreement on checklist interpretation or ordering) and subsequent convergence (adherence to a moderator's resolution rule) while still merely tracking the right answer via checklist compliance, without any genuine error-correction mechanism. The target also fails to address the problem's requirement for a single evaluation: it provides no metric or observable that a lone evaluator could apply to separate genuine reliability from coincidental compliance.
